purpose: Foundational hireable factions and regional world-state identities.

entities.name: The Cinder March Covenant

identity.fantasy: A mobile nation of furnace cities, ash rangers, oathbound siege captains, and monster hunters who treat every frontier as a temporary battlefield.
identity.silhouette: Black iron, ember-orange cloth, portable banners, furnace vents, hooked rifles, and scorched heraldry built around a broken sun.
identity.lore_hook: The Covenant advances only into lands that have already been declared uninhabitable, arguing that civilization is strongest where survival was supposed to be impossible.

signature: Marching Citadels periodically relocate faction services between authored frontier hubs.
Ash Oaths unlock contract branches based on whether players rescue, hunt, fortify, or conquer.
Cinder Reprisal increases local faction patrol strength after repeated attacks against Covenant holdings.
counterplay: Their caravans create visible logistics routes that enemies can disrupt; territorial gains require sustained supply.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Ember banners shed ash without burning, furnace convoys leave glowing wheel-runes, and major Covenant events tint smoke columns deep orange across the local skyline.
animation: Faction NPCs use drilled shield-and-rifle formations, ritual weapon salutes, and synchronized caravan deployment animations that emphasize military discipline.
audio: Heavy marching drums, forge hammers used as rhythmic signals, low horn calls for caravan movement, and sharp whistle codes during hunts.

method: Faction reputation is earned through authored contracts, rescues, world events, and faction-specific mastery.

entities.name: The Meridian Null Cartel

identity.fantasy: Spies, cartographers, smugglers, and portal thieves who traffic in forbidden routes, erased maps, and places that officially do not exist.
identity.silhouette: Midnight coats, mirrored masks, animated coordinate lines, compact portal hardware, and map-scroll fabrics that redraw themselves.
identity.lore_hook: The Cartel became wealthy by selling shortcuts through wars, then became powerful enough that governments began paying them to forget certain roads existed.

signature: Black Atlas routes temporarily expose authored traversal shortcuts when sufficient Cartel reputation is held.
Null Auctions exchange intelligence tokens for rare location data rather than direct combat power.
Erased Territory events make selected POI entrances shift between multiple authored access states.
counterplay: Cartel routes can be compromised, and using hostile shortcuts can trigger ambush contracts or reputation loss.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Thin black compass roses bloom on surfaces, route seams glow like erased pencil lines, and portal hardware emits flat mirror-like distortions instead of colorful rifts.
animation: Agents constantly scan corners, fold maps into impossible shapes, and use compact hand signs to coordinate before portal breaches.
audio: Pen scratches, reversed compass clicks, soft sonar inversions, and whispered coordinate strings layered beneath ambient sound.

entities.name: The Verdant Teeth

identity.fantasy: A militant ecological order that bonds with monsters, breeds living weapons, and views cities as temporary infestations inside a much older food chain.
identity.silhouette: Living thorn armor, luminous seed organs, bone-and-vine weapons, beast masks, and enormous tameable predators used as mobile shrines.
identity.lore_hook: The Verdant Teeth believe every creature has a place in the ecosystem—including civilization, provided civilization remembers it can still be eaten.

signature: Predator Accord changes eligible wildlife disposition based on regional faction reputation.
Bloom War causes authored plant structures to grow into cover, traps, or traversal during faction events.
Apex Pilgrimage sends players across multiple biomes to bond with progressively more dangerous creatures.
Living Arsenal crafting converts monster-derived materials into faction-specific biological equipment.
counterplay: Fire, corruption, and overhunting can destabilize their regional ecology and close certain services until restored.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Bioluminescent spores trace faction paths, thorn structures visibly grow from seed points, bonded beasts display changing crest patterns, and faction hubs pulse like living organs.
animation: Members use animal-like crouches, vine-assisted vaults, seed-planting gestures, and calm open-palmed taming rituals even around enormous predators.
audio: Wet vine snaps, layered insect harmonics, distant animal calls used as signals, and deep wooden resonance when major bonds complete.

entities.name: The Cathedral of Iron Mercy

identity.fantasy: Knight-engineers, plague wardens, relic smiths, and battlefield medics who convert corruption into armor, power, and containment structures.
identity.silhouette: Cathedral plate, reliquary shields, molten scripture, iron bells, red-white cloth, and mobile chapels mounted on armored vehicles.
identity.lore_hook: The Cathedral teaches that corruption cannot always be destroyed, but it can be forced to pay rent in the form of useful energy.

signature: Mercy Furnaces consume authored corruption resources to power regional defenses.
Sanctuary Lines create temporary safe corridors during invasion events when faction objectives remain intact.
Reliquary Forging unlocks anti-corruption armor branches from purified boss materials.
Bell Judgment events repel or enrage necrotic populations depending on player choices.
counterplay: Their defenses are resource hungry; destroying or starving Mercy Furnaces sharply reduces regional protection.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Molten scripture crawls across architecture, corruption burns into silver sparks at sanctuary borders, and giant translucent cathedral-window patterns appear during successful cleanses.
animation: Wardens advance behind shields in measured formations, medics use heavy reliquary tools, and smith-priests hammer glowing symbols directly into armor plates.
audio: Deep iron bells, restrained choir textures, furnace hiss, heavy shield impacts, and clear warning tolls before containment failures.

entities.name: The Blacktide Dominion

identity.fantasy: An oceanic military civilization operating through drowned transit systems, abyssal fortresses, pressure weapons, and amphibious assault companies.
identity.silhouette: Black-blue scale armor, pressure tanks, manta fins, harpoon rifles, wet reflective capes, and vehicles shaped like predatory marine life.
identity.lore_hook: The Dominion's capital sank generations ago; instead of rebuilding above water, they declared the sea itself to be their road network and expanded.

signature: Drowned Transit unlocks fast travel through submerged authored tunnels as reputation rises.
Pressure Front assaults can flood or drain selected encounter sub-areas in staged scripted transitions.
Abyssal Salvage contracts recover rare vehicle and weapon components from dangerous wreck zones.
counterplay: Dominion technology loses efficiency in dry inland strongholds, and transit routes can be sealed by rival factions.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Black current ribbons mark movement lanes, pressure doors bloom with blue-white condensation, and faction assaults send wall-like water shadows racing across nearby surfaces.
animation: Troops use low hydrodynamic movement, cable-braced firing stances, coordinated dive entries, and shoulder-first breach animations through pressure doors.
audio: Muffled sub-bass booms, sonar knocks, cable whine, pressure pops, and distant foghorn calls used as military signals.

entities.name: The Court of Broken Hours

identity.fantasy: Chronarchs, ruined nobles, state archivists, and time duelists who manipulate recorded authored states, delayed actions, and ritualized timing windows.
identity.silhouette: Fractured clock armor, transparent gear plates, floating hour hands, silver-black regalia, and trailing afterimages that lag behind physical movement.
identity.lore_hook: The Court survived the destruction of its kingdom by refusing to agree on which moment the destruction actually occurred.

signature: Chronicle Vaults preserve encounter records used to unlock replay challenges and mastery rewards.
Ruined Hour events alter timing windows and enemy sequencing without unrestricted global time control.
Court Duels reward precision timing, parries, and synchronized team execution instead of raw DPS.
Archive Verdicts change faction reputation based on whether players preserve or intentionally destroy recorded histories.
counterplay: Protected world states cannot be rewound; Court mechanics are telegraphed and vulnerable to disruption at anchors.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Transparent clock rails cross the environment, afterimages stack at key positions, numeral fragments orbit important anchors, and successful state restores snap through layered ghost poses.
animation: Court members move with deliberate pauses followed by sudden synchronized motion, rotate wrist-mounted time rings before casts, and use formal dueling bows before high-stakes challenges.
audio: Multiple asynchronous ticking layers, reversed bells, metronome-like combat cues, and a single enormous clock strike during major state transitions.

entities.name: The Hollow Astral Synod

identity.fantasy: Astronomers, void navigators, star-render artillery priests, and dimensional scholars who map places between stars and weaponize controlled absence.
identity.silhouette: White-black astral robes over hard armor, floating astrolabes, starfield masks, negative-space ornaments, and thin luminous coordinate grids.
identity.lore_hook: The Synod does not worship the stars; it considers stars to be instruments for measuring the shape of everything missing between them.

signature: Astral Batteries charge regional observatories used for high-tier event support.
Void Survey missions reveal unstable dimensional pockets with rotating hazards and rare materials.
Synod Alignment events let players choose which observatory network receives power, changing available support abilities.
Star-Render Protocols unlock carefully telegraphed orbital encounter mechanics in open-sky regions.
counterplay: Observatories are fixed strategic assets, and many Synod systems become unavailable underground or when alignment infrastructure is destroyed.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Star maps crawl across terrain, floating astrolabes cast thin geometric shadows, void anchors appear as perfect black disks, and artillery alignments paint enormous constellation lanes across the sky.
animation: Researchers manipulate floating instruments with precise finger motions, artillery priests perform slow alignment gestures, and void navigators move with tiny spatial skips near active anchors.
audio: Deep celestial ticks, glass harmonics, low gravitational hum, distant radio-like star noise, and descending tones before artillery impacts.

entities.name: The Last Gate Imperium
entities.role: fortress civilization and oathbound rescue order

identity.fantasy: A civilization built around defensive mastery, rescue doctrine, siege endurance, and the belief that abandoning an ally is a metaphysical crime.
identity.silhouette: Fortress-shaped helms, rectangular blade-shields, ivory gunmetal armor, city-name inscriptions, and mobile gate structures deployed as battlefield cover.
identity.lore_hook: The Imperium formed after an ancient evacuation failed; every law it writes is ultimately a variation on one promise: nobody is left beyond the gate.

signature: Gate Oaths track successful rescues, defended objectives, and squad survival to unlock deeper faction standing.
Moving Bastions deploy temporary cover routes during world events and retreat as objectives fall.
Imperial Burden contracts reward players for absorbing risk on behalf of weaker squads or NPC populations.
Last Gate sieges become multi-stage regional events where failure changes local faction control.
counterplay: Their formations are powerful but predictable; separating defenders from their bastions reduces their advantage.
evolution: Faction standing unlocks deeper services, contracts, visual recognition, and region-specific world-state influence.

vfx: Towering translucent gate outlines rise during defensive events, temporary ally names illuminate on shields after rescues, and moving bastions project clean ivory geometry onto the ground.
animation: Imperial units plant shields in synchronized walls, physically carry injured NPCs, form rotating cover teams, and kneel in massive oath ceremonies after successful sieges.
audio: Stone gate groans, command horns, layered shield impacts, whispered names of defended settlements, and monumental closing-gate booms.

method: Faction reputation is earned through authored contracts, rescues, world events, and faction-specific mastery.
